A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PILoT and the same implicit-sparsification framework. All 20 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original synthetic linear-recovery experiments and CIFAR10/CIFAR100 pruning results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original linear-recovery, CIFAR and ImageNet experiments, including additional pruning and label-smoothing comparisons.

M1.justification: The parameterization, initialization principle and weight-decay objective are retained. Beyond v1's fixed strengths and simple schedules, v2 introduces a substantive feedback controller: Algorithm 1 adjusts regularization multiplicatively using training accuracy and an L1 threshold, then enforces decay during the second half of training.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet classification experiments for one-shot and iterative pruning, substantially extending the empirical coverage beyond synthetic recovery and CIFAR10/CIFAR100. The CIFAR iterative experiments remain in Appendix C.3.

E2.justification: The CIFAR one-shot comparison adds evaluated STR and removes the displayed sigmoid-mask Continuous Sparsification, Powerpropagation and mask-only L1 comparisons. The linear-recovery comparison also drops mask-only regularization and directly contrasts PILoT with spred and LASSO; spred itself was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: CIFAR10 regularization tuning expands from v1's listed strengths around 10^-4–10^-3 to 10^-5–10^-2. New ImageNet protocols include iterative pruning with batch size 512, 90 epochs per cycle and 10 warmup epochs. The additional experiment without label smoothing also changes PILoT's effective-weight L2 penalty and threshold K.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ImageNet analysis without label smoothing, although PILoT is also retuned, limiting isolation of smoothing's effect. It removes the batch-size-5 stochastic recovery study in v1 Figure 5 and the unregularized CIFAR iterative-pruning variants, while revising the initialization and schedule comparisons.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly states three seeds and 95% confidence intervals across experiments, with a separate one-shot seed disclosure. V2 retains five initializations and 95% regions for linear recovery and three seeds for iterative pruning, but omits comparable one-shot disclosures. This establishes reduced reporting, not fewer actual runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial ImageNet results: Table 1 reports 68.49% top-1 accuracy for PILoT versus 66.12% for spred at 97.19% sparsity. It also adds results without label smoothing and ImageNet iterative-pruning curves. CIFAR one-shot results are revised under changed tuning and scheduling, while stochastic-recovery and several variant results disappear; these are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: Most theorems and proofs are retained across relocation. V2 adds the spred specialization and sign-preservation reasoning in Section 3, tightens the main mirror-flow theorem's initialization condition from non-strict to strict inequality, and explicitly defines a coordinate-minimum constant in the convergence rate.

C1.justification: The core claims about controllable implicit sparsification, convergence and linear-regression optimality remain. V2 adds an explicit sign-flip contribution and qualifies the introductory hierarchical optimization formulation around attaining zero training loss.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the mechanism explanation through delayed L2-to-L1 sparsification, magnitude-dependent updates versus STR, and spred's sign restrictions under gradient flow. It qualifies those restrictions for practical training with large steps or noise and explicitly acknowledges that PILoT is not state of the art at moderate ImageNet sparsity with label smoothing.

D1.justification: V2 supplies controller settings such as delta=1.01 and K=8000 for CIFAR, per-sparsity ImageNet configurations, effective-weight regularization details and STR's threshold initialization. Appendix C.2 also newly documents validation-based configuration selection. These substantially expand implementation information beyond v1's existing hyperparameter and hardware disclosures.

R1.justification: V2 adds sparse-recovery and group-sparsity references, including works by Vaškevičius, Li and Zhao, plus ImageNet and weight-rewinding references. It sharpens positioning against STR and spred while retaining the broader sparsification and mirror-flow literature framework.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, motivation and theoretical exposition. Much of v1 Section 2 moves to Appendix A, a dedicated algorithm section is introduced, and CIFAR iterative experiments move to the appendix. Citation style and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: V2 separates and redesigns v1 Figure 1, replaces the crowded CIFAR one-shot display, and relocates a reduced CIFAR iterative figure. It adds ImageNet result and configuration tables, an iterative-pruning figure and an algorithm box, alongside substantial page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: V1 leaves the practical scheduling rule underspecified and evaluates only synthetic/CIFAR settings. V2 provides an explicit adaptive controller, substantially more implementation detail and ImageNet comparisons against STR/spred and iterative pruning. These materially strengthen reproducibility and evidence of practical utility. The removed stochastic analysis, weaker one-shot uncertainty disclosure and confounded label-smoothing comparison are meaningful losses, but do not outweigh those gains.
